summary: Focused end-to-end validation of the new Analysis History feature. Backend: 3/3 pytest cases passed - GET /api/competitors/{id}/history returns 5 chronological snapshots (oldest->newest) with upward overall trend and all required fields (date, overall, scores{}, starting_price, confidence, feature_count); POST /api/competitors/{id}/analyze appends exactly one new snapshot; DELETE /api/competitors/{id} cascades and removes history (subsequent history GET returns 404). Frontend: Logged in as admin@example.com/admin123, opened Competitors -> View (data-testid=view-Slack), Analysis History modal renders with data-testid=analysis-history containing LineChart SVG, metric selector (data-testid=history-metric-select), trend badge ("▲ 10 pts"), and 6 snapshot rows (data-testid=history-row-0..5, 6 because backend re-analyze test appended one). Changing metric selector from Overall to Innovation updates chart data, trend badge (▲ 22 pts), and per-row displayed value. All acceptance criteria met.
critical_code_review_comments: demo_data.build_demo_history seeds 5 snapshots but the newest snapshot is generated at datetime.now() while the competitor's last_analyzed is hardcoded to _NOW='2026-06-01' - the header date and history newest-date can look inconsistent (e.g., competitor shows 2026-06-01 but newest history date is today). Consider aligning last_analyzed with the newest snapshot date or vice versa.
GET /api/competitors/{cid}/history returns up to 500 items via to_list(500) with no pagination - fine for now but should paginate if snapshot volume grows.
_record_history writes on every successful analyze but does not dedupe/rate-limit; rapid repeated analyze calls will bloat history.
seed_data_creation: None. Used existing demo Slack competitor. Ephemeral 'TEST_HistDel' competitor created and deleted within delete test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Analysis History feature verified end-to-end. Note: after running these backend tests, the demo Slack competitor may have 6 history snapshots (5 seeded + 1 from test_reanalyze_appends_snapshot). Test file at /app/backend/tests/test_history.py is idempotent and reusable.
